gas-tx-caption: How gas moves in a message call, drawn as a fuel rig: the sender's pump fills a tank to the gas limit, the contract's engine burns what its code uses, and unused fuel flows back through a meter.
gas-tx-description: A transaction enters the world state. Its sender, an externally owned account, reserves a gas supply equal to the transaction's gas limit. A message carries the call to a contract account, whose EVM code runs and burns gas for each operation. When execution finishes, the unused gas, which is the gas limit minus the gas used, flows back to the externally owned account as a refund. If execution runs out of gas, all of the reserved gas is consumed, the contract's state changes are reverted, and nothing is returned.
diagram-readout-label: Gas for this example, in gas units
gas-tx-step-idle: Pick an example and send the transaction to follow its gas step by step.
gas-tx-step-enter: Step {step}: the transaction enters the world state with a gas limit of {limit} gas.
gas-tx-step-reserve: Step {step}: the externally owned account reserves the full {limit} gas as the gas supply.
gas-tx-step-execute: Step {step}: the message reaches the contract account, and its EVM code runs and burns {used} gas.
gas-tx-step-execute-out-of-gas: Step {step}: the EVM code needs more than {limit} gas, so it runs out of gas, burns all {limit} and fails.
gas-tx-step-return: Step {step}: the {returned} unused gas flows back to the externally owned account as a refund.
gas-tx-step-revert: Step {step}: the contract's state changes are reverted, and no gas is returned.
gas-tx-definition-deck: The state of every account: balances, nonces, code and storage.
gas-tx-definition-order: The signed transaction. It sets the gas limit the call may spend.
gas-tx-definition-pump: The externally owned account that sends the transaction, pays for gas and gets unused gas back.
gas-tx-definition-tank: The gas limit, reserved before the code runs and drained as gas is used.
gas-tx-definition-feed: The message call, carried from the sender to the contract.
gas-tx-definition-engine: The contract account. Its EVM code uses gas for every operation it runs.
gas-tx-definition-return-line: Gas the call didn't use, flowing back to the sender.
gas-tx-definition-meter: How much unused gas goes back to the sender.
gas-evm-caption: Where gas goes inside the EVM: the transaction first pays a fixed intrinsic cost, then every operation draws its own cost from the gas supply. Stack and memory work is cheap; writing to storage costs the most.
gas-evm-description: A gas supply feeds the EVM through a pipe. Before any code runs, the transaction pays {intrinsic} gas of intrinsic cost. Then the program counter steps through seven opcodes: two PUSH1 put {value} and {slot} on the stack, MSTORE writes {value} to memory, two more PUSH1, then SSTORE writes {value} to a new storage slot, and STOP ends the run. Each opcode draws its cost from the supply; SSTORE alone costs {sstore} gas. With too little gas, execution runs out at SSTORE: all the gas is consumed and the write is reverted.
gas-evm-step-idle: Pick an example, then step through the code or run it.
gas-evm-step-intrinsic: Step {step}: before any code runs, the transaction pays {intrinsic} gas of intrinsic cost.
gas-evm-step-push1: PUSH1 puts {value} on the stack: {cost} gas.
gas-evm-step-mstore: MSTORE writes {value} to memory, growing it by one word: {cost} gas.
gas-evm-step-sstore: SSTORE writes {value} to a new storage slot, the most expensive kind of write: {cost} gas.
gas-evm-step-stop: STOP ends the run: {used} gas used, {left} gas left to return.
gas-evm-step-out-of-gas: SSTORE needs {cost} gas but only {left} is left, so the call runs out of gas: all {limit} gas is consumed and the write is reverted.
gas-evm-definition-deck: The plate everything stands on: the state of every account. Only storage on it persists after the call.
gas-evm-definition-tank: The gas limit bought for the transaction. Intrinsic gas and every opcode draw from it.
gas-evm-definition-evm: The Ethereum Virtual Machine. Its program counter steps through the contract's code, one opcode at a time.
gas-evm-definition-stack: Short-lived working values. Pushing one costs {cost} gas.
gas-evm-definition-memory: Scratch space for the call, cleared when it ends. Cheap, but growing it costs a little extra.
gas-evm-definition-storage: The contract's persistent state. Writing a new slot costs {cost} gas, far more than anything else here.
gas-tx-status-idle: Ready: pick an example and send it
gas-evm-status-idle: Ready: pick an example and run it
gas-evm-status-out-of-gas: Out of gas at SSTORE: write reverted
